headline: Google DeepMind releases Gemma, a new open-weight LLM library.

items.title: Gemma Gem – AI model embedded in a browser – no API keys, no cloud
items.summary: Gemma Gem is a Chrome extension that loads Google's Gemma 4 (2B) through WebGPU in an offscreen document and provides tools for interacting with webpages, like reading content, taking screenshots, and executing JavaScript. This tool offers a chat overlay on every page for user interaction.

items.title: Gemma open-weight LLM library
items.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemma, an open-weight library for large language models (LLMs). This library is designed to facilitate easier experimentation and deployment of LLMs by developers, offering a high degree of customization and integration capabilities.

items.title: microsoft/agent-framework
items.summary: Microsoft's agent-framework is a new tool for building, orchestrating, and deploying AI agents and multi-agent workflows. It supports Python and .NET, allowing developers to create complex AI-driven applications with ease.

items.title: Blaizzy/mlx-vlm
items.summary: MLX-VLM is a package for inference and fine-tuning of Vision Language Models (VLMs) on Mac systems, leveraging the MLX framework for enhanced performance in multimodal tasks.

items.title: Understanding the Nature of Generative AI as Threshold Logic in High-Dimensional Space
items.summary: This research paper examines the role of threshold logic in understanding generative AI. The study provides a transparent model of neural computation, contributing to a deeper understanding of how generative models operate.

items.title: Xpertbench: Expert Level Tasks with Rubrics-Based Evaluation
items.summary: Xpertbench introduces a new evaluation framework for LLMs that assesses their proficiency in complex, open-ended tasks, moving beyond traditional benchmarks to better measure expert-level cognition.

items.title: Show HN: I built a tiny LLM to demystify how language models work
items.summary: A developer created a small-scale LLM with approximately 9 million parameters using a vanilla transformer model and synthetic data, aimed at understanding the internal workings of language models. The project is open-source and available for experimentation and customization.

all_items.title: Show HN: I built a tiny LLM to demystify how language models work
all_items.summary:
Built a ~9M param LLM from scratch to understand how they actually work. Vanilla transformer, 60K synthetic conversations, ~130 lines of PyTorch. Trains in 5 min on a free Colab T4. The fish thinks the meaning of life is food.

Fork it and swap the personality for your own character.

all_items.summary: arXiv:2604.02546v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Pretraining 3D encoders by aligning with Contrastive Language Image Pretraining (CLIP) has emerged as a promising direction to learn generalizable representations for 3D scene understanding.
